newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmakers hear Twins stadium proposals.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmakers hear Twins stadium proposals.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson wants legislators to reach a decision on a proposed new stadium for the Twins without resorting to a special session, a spokesman for the governor said Thursday.
Lawmakers are faced with a May 19 deadline for approving the state's biennium budget, possible flood damage relief and the stadium among other issues.
Even conceding that, however, the stadium issue has been before legislators for some time and Carlson believes they should address it in the time available, spokesman Brian Dietz said.
"The legislature has had this issue the last two years, knowing they had to get something done, there is no reason why they shouldn't get it done this year," Dietz said.

Legislators met in a joint house and senate tax committee hearing for much of Wednesday listening to proponents and opponents of a new ballpark, which could cost $400 million or more if it includes a retractable roof.
They have set an informal deadline of May 9 to move proposals beyond the committees for debate by the house and senate.
The Star Tribune reported Thursday that acting baseball commissioner Bud Selig told the committee members the Twins franchise likely would be forced to leave Minnesota without a new stadium.
On Tuesday, Minnesota senate republicans announced that they would back a proposal to put video slot machines at a racetrack near the Twin Cities to help pay for a new stadium.

Carl Pohlad, the Twins owner, has agreed to contribute $15 million cash to a new stadium and $25 million generated through naming rights and other ballpark-related revenues. He also would agree to allowing the state 49 percent interest in the club.
